owner_decisions.reason: Cargo workspace remains UNLICENSED and publish=false, so OSS release basis cannot be declared by Runtime implementation alone.

classifications.title: Runtime Release debt reaudit
evidence: README, Product Charter, Product Completion Gate, Runtime Boundary DoD, Brownie Scope, Runtime Protocol, CLI External Loop, Task Runtime, Tool Execution, Permission Gate, ModePack specs, current phase-value manifest, M64.15 manifest, control-plane pointer, Rust crates, Node guards, VSIX check path, and CI workflow were reaudited.
This audit is now machine-checked by scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.mjs and human-readable in docs/architecture/runtime-release-readiness-audit.md.
classifications.next_action: Use this artifact as the bounded source for the remaining P0/P1 closure phases.

classifications.title: Boundary Protocol gaps
evidence: Runtime boundary docs define Run Request, Runtime Event, Control Command, and Run Result/Attestation.
RRP-1 adds docs/architecture/runtime-boundary-canonical-contract.json as the canonical public Runtime boundary contract and compatibility matrix.

scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.mjs validates required Runtime boundary surfaces, required public method subset, CLI/VSIX/Runtime/spec anchors, compatibility-matrix entries, and non-authority language through the existing VSIX-invoked release-readiness guard path.
classifications.next_action: Use the canonical Runtime boundary contract as the guarded source for public boundary compatibility while closing the remaining Runtime Release Readiness blockers.

classifications.title: Cancel semantics
evidence: RRP-2 adds a Runtime-owned task.cancel JSON-RPC boundary with typed protocol params and result.

task.cancel requires caller authorization, concrete task/run identity, expected current status, expected task updated_at, bounded cancel_id, and a Runtime-computed cancel request fingerprint before terminal evidence.
Only Created, Queued, and Running tasks are cancellable; missing, stale, mismatched, completed, failed, malformed, ambiguous, or unrelated requests fail closed before TaskCancelled evidence.
Exact replay is idempotent only when the current durable TaskCancelled payload matches the same cancel request fingerprint; otherwise cancelled tasks fail closed without duplicate terminal evidence.
VSIX protocol validators and runtime client projections cover task.cancel params/results while remaining thin transport validation over Runtime authority.
classifications.next_action: Use task.cancel as the explicit Runtime-owned cancellation boundary while closing the remaining Runtime Release Readiness blockers.

classifications.title: Real process loss Recovery E2E
evidence: RRP-3 replaces create_new MCP approval claim lock authority with an OS-owned advisory file lock over a non-authoritative residual lock file.
headless.run.recovery_probe invokes Runtime-owned unfinished MCP approval recovery and converts latest executing approval state to outcome_unknown with bounded fingerprint evidence exactly once.
Focused runtime tests cover stale residual lock file progress, executing-to-outcome_unknown recovery idempotence, and no tools/call replay from outcome_unknown.

test:rrp3-process-loss launches actual brownie-runtime child processes with an isolated trusted active Mode Pack snapshot and deterministic fake MCP stdio server, kills/restarts Runtime mid-call, verifies stale lock progress, executing-before-spawn recovery, outcome_unknown idempotence, independent process racing with at most one tools/call, and terminal consumed non-rerun after restart.
classifications.next_action: Use RRP-3 process-loss evidence as the local Runtime recovery baseline while closing the remaining Runtime Release Readiness blockers.

classifications.title: Durable schema version and migration
evidence: Protocol, ModePack, AgentModes, CLI automation, MCP, and journey snapshots carry schema_version fields.
No release-level durable store schema version and forward migration gate was found for task/run/journey/checkpoint/ledger state.
classifications.next_action: Add explicit durable schema version and migration/fail-closed behavior in the migration phase.

classifications.title: CI Release Gate
evidence: The existing CI still uses pnpm install instead of pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and does not directly run every release-relevant guard test.
RRD-1 wires the Runtime release readiness guard into the VSIX check path that CI already invokes.

The Runtime release readiness guard now supports audit-driven convergence: open Runtime P0/P1 debt keeps runtime_release_ready=false, closed Runtime blockers must be removed from release_ready_blocked_by, and all closed Runtime blockers require runtime_release_ready=true.
Full CI Release Gate hardening remains a later P0 closure phase because workflow update authority was unavailable.
classifications.next_action: Close the remaining CI workflow hardening when workflow update authority is available.

classifications.title: MCP Runtime Safety Policy finite closure
evidence: The user supplied a non-conflicting follow-on MCP Runtime Safety Policy campaign after RRD-1.

MCP-S1 closes result error semantics, MCP-S1.1 corrects CallToolResult resultType/isError protocol-conformance edge cases, MCP-S2 closes tool-level Brownie safety policy, MCP-S3 closes annotation provenance/drift checks, MCP-S4 closes tool-level approval binding, MCP-S4.1 closes approval consumption/retry safety, MCP-S5 closes runtime input/output schema validation, MCP-S6 closes the secret reference contract, and MCP-S7 closes executable identity.

MCP stdio execution is now result-safe, policy-bound, annotation/catalog drift checked, approval-state-bound, schema-validated, secret-reference scoped, and executable-identity pinned and rechecked before launch.

MCP approval-required execution uses public mcp.tool.approve, Runtime-owned latest-state approval claims, consumed/outcome_unknown terminalization, and duplicate retry/reuse denial from durable attempt evidence.
MCP server descriptions, schemas, annotations, results, secret references, executable identity, approval state, and model output remain non-authoritative and narrowing-only.
classifications.next_action: Continue the remaining Runtime Release Readiness P0/P1 blockers before claiming Runtime Release Ready.

classifications.title: OSS Release technical basis
evidence: Workspace Cargo.toml declares license = UNLICENSED and publish = false.
Runtime can prepare technical release evidence, but license/publish posture requires owner decision before OSS Release Ready can be claimed.
classifications.next_action: Record owner license/publish decision before declaring OSS release basis complete.

classifications.title: Protocol/Event canonization
evidence: Runtime events and protocol structs exist in brownie-protocol, brownie-events, brownie-store, runtime, CLI, and VSIX projection code.
Release needs a canonical event/protocol ownership map and guard against drift between Rust protocol, runtime JSON-RPC handlers, CLI validation, VSIX validation, and docs.
classifications.next_action: Canonize protocol/event ownership and drift tests in the protocol/event phase.

classifications.title: Runtime module decomposition reevaluation
evidence: M64.15 explicitly left runtime-module-decomposition open after partial closure.
crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains very large and owns multiple release-critical protocol, admission, execution, recovery, and completion seams.
classifications.next_action: Reevaluate module boundaries with behavior-preserving extraction only where it reduces release risk.

classifications.title: Platform, deadline, and durability hardening
evidence: Runtime owns execution budgets, stale conflict behavior, recovery probes, and durable state boundaries.

Release needs a bounded audit and tests for deadline propagation, crash-safe write ordering, fsync/atomicity assumptions, platform path handling, and failure classification within local Runtime scope.
classifications.next_action: Harden only Runtime-owned local durability and deadline semantics, not hosted platform products.

classifications.title: Hosted scheduler, daemon, job queue, and worker fleet
evidence: README, Brownie Scope, Product Charter, and Runtime Boundary DoD classify schedulers, daemons, worker fleets, leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLAs, and billing outside Brownie Runtime release.

classifications.title: Forge and notification adapters
evidence: GitHub/GitLab Apps, PR create/update/merge workflows, Slack/Teams/email, SIEM, OTel, and customer-system adapters are external adapter readiness, not Runtime release blockers.
classifications.next_action: Track as adapter product work only after Runtime release closure.

classifications.title: Enterprise, Assurance, and commercial solution readiness
evidence: Tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, customer admin UI, billing, certified stack, continuity assurance, and broad BDK/Enterprise/Assurance surfaces are outside this Runtime-owned campaign.
classifications.next_action: Do not use these items to block Brownie Runtime release.
